html:
An Italian Jesuit priest who lived in Ming China from 1582 until his death in Beijing in 1610. He was a founder of the Jesuit mission there.

Ricci arrived through Macau and spent years learning the language and the classics. He first dressed as a Buddhist monk, then switched to the robes of a Confucian scholar once he saw who held respect. He argued that Confucius was compatible with Christianity, and allowed converts to keep honouring their ancestors. That approach was later fought over in the Chinese Rites controversy.

He won over scholars with Western science: clocks, astronomy and maps. His world map of 1602, printed in Chinese, placed China near the centre and showed Chinese readers the Americas. With the convert official Xu Guangqi he translated the first books of Euclid's Elements. In 1601 he reached Beijing and was allowed to stay. When he died, the emperor granted him a burial plot there, a rare honour for a foreigner.
sum: An Italian Jesuit priest who lived in Ming China from 1582 until his death in Beijing in 1610. He was a founder of the Jesuit mission there.
